In the current year, productivity and growth initiatives accounted for 44% of investment spend. The Bank is continuing its focus on strengthening our capabilities and extending our leadership in digital, technology and customer-centric product offerings through ongoing modernisation of our platforms and interfaces to provide integrated and personalised experiences for our customers. The Bank is also continuing to invest in initiatives to simplify and enhance our systems, automate and digitise processes, and uplift internal engineering capabilities.

Infrastructure and branch refurbishment initiatives accounted for 26% of investment spend, an increase of 3% from 23% in the prior year, with the Bank continuing to uplift cyber security and enhance IT infrastructure including the accelerated refresh of critical legacy technology platforms.
• Simplifying and automating manual back-end processes and systems including the use of Generative AI models to improve customer experience, reduce operating costs and digitise end-to-end processes;

summary_statements.text: CBA reported total investment spending of 2,297 AUD million in FY2025, compared with 2,010 AUD million in FY2024. That is an increase of 287 AUD million (14.28%, calculated and rounded).
The largest disclosed category in FY2025 was Productivity and growth at 1,023 AUD million. The biggest year-on-year increase was Infrastructure and branch refurbishment, up 128 AUD million.
The fastest percentage growth was Infrastructure and branch refurbishment at 27.47% (calculated and rounded). Rankings apply only to these three disclosed investment categories.
Productivity and growth: 926 AUD million in FY2024 to 1,023 AUD million in FY2025.
Risk and compliance: 618 AUD million in FY2024 to 680 AUD million in FY2025.
Infrastructure and branch refurbishment: 466 AUD million in FY2024 to 594 AUD million in FY2025.

CBA describes its direction as follows: "In the current year, productivity and growth initiatives accounted for 44% of investment spend. The Bank is continuing its focus on strengthening our capabilities and extending our leadership in digital, technology and customer-centric product offerings through ongoing modernisation of our platforms and interfaces to provide integrated and personalised experiences for our customers. The Bank is also continuing to invest in initiatives to simplify and enhance our systems, automate and digitise processes, and uplift internal engineering capabilities."

Question scope: CBA / FY2025

CBA reported total investment spending of 2,297 AUD million in FY2025, compared with 2,010 AUD million in FY2024. That is an increase of 287 AUD million (14.28%, calculated and rounded). [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

The largest disclosed category in FY2025 was Productivity and growth at 1,023 AUD million. The biggest year-on-year increase was Infrastructure and branch refurbishment, up 128 AUD million. [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

The fastest percentage growth was Infrastructure and branch refurbishment at 27.47% (calculated and rounded). Rankings apply only to these three disclosed investment categories. [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

Productivity and growth: 926 AUD million in FY2024 to 1,023 AUD million in FY2025. [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

Risk and compliance: 618 AUD million in FY2024 to 680 AUD million in FY2025. [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

Infrastructure and branch refurbishment: 466 AUD million in FY2024 to 594 AUD million in FY2025. [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

CBA describes its direction as follows: "In the current year, productivity and growth initiatives accounted for 44% of investment spend. The Bank is continuing its focus on strengthening our capabilities and extending our leadership in digital, technology and customer-centric product offerings through ongoing modernisation of our platforms and interfaces to provide integrated and personalised experiences for our customers. The Bank is also continuing to invest in initiatives to simplify and enhance our systems, automate and digitise processes, and uplift internal engineering capabilities." [CBA FY2025 Profit Announcement, PDF page 32]

Interpreting investment as spending on CBA's own business. These figures describe CBA Group investment spending on a continuing-operations basis, not lending to industries, total IT operating expenses or an AI-only budget. Technology projects span multiple categories.
